source: Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries (MAFF), General Directorate of Agriculture, Department of Agricultural Extension — 'បច្ចេកទេសដាំដំណាំឪឡឹក' (Watermelon Cultivation Techniques), 2017.
text:
Before sowing in the nursery, seed can be treated in one of two ways to protect it from soil-borne fungal disease: (1) soak the seed in warm water for about 30 minutes at roughly 1:2:3 hot-to-cold water ratio, or (2) soak/treat the seed in a fungicide solution such as Captan 50% WP at a rate of about 25 to 30 grams per liter of water for around 2 to 3 hours before sowing, which helps protect the germinating seed from damping-off and other seedling diseases.

Seed is sown into nursery trays (plastic seedling trays with individual cells) filled with a prepared growing medium (a mix that typically includes topsoil, well-decomposed manure/compost, rice husk ash or burnt rice hull, and fine sand or a similar loosening material), pressed level and gently watered before sowing so the medium is evenly moist. One seed is placed per cell/hole, pressed in and lightly covered with medium; care should be taken not to bury the seed too deep, which can prevent normal germination.

Seedling trays are then watered gently (a fine spray or drip so as not to dislodge the seed) once or twice daily depending on weather, keeping the medium moist but not waterlogged. Watermelon seedlings are generally ready and old enough to transplant to the field about 7 to 8 days after sowing/emergence, once they have developed roughly 2 to 3 true leaves; seedlings should be transplanted promptly once they reach this stage, since delaying transplanting can weaken the seedlings.
